items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: you know I worked with Herbie Mann a little bit and then Les McCann and then Eddie Harris.

ctx.x: That was the first record I made that sold you know. And I would come to his sessions you know, so I’d see him do the MJQ or Herbie Mann or Hank Crawford or Betty Carter. And I was kind of learning as I went along. I didn’t know what I was doing. And when I saw that he was less and less involved in producing jazz, and then when he called me to come to New York and I had no idea what he wanted, and he said, “you know that job you want? Well you’ve got it.” And he said, “I love you, you’re a nice kid” all of that.…

Allison, you know I worked with Herbie Mann a little bit and then Les McCann and then Eddie Harris. So when he hired me he said, “I’m not in the clubs anymore, this isn’t my time, this is your time, so go get ‘em.”
When you said I’ve got some new ideas, you take an artist who’s already established or semi-established, what kind of ideas would you present to that artist?
